record.hypothesis: For all four datasets, apply smooth norm compression to tied item embeddings: e_eff=e/sqrt(1+||e||²), with padding exactly zero. Use the same transformation for history and candidate lookups, retaining dimension 64 and the existing input multiplier. Unlike hard unit normalization, this preserves magnitude differences among small embeddings while limiting large norms. Keep HSTU topology, positions, history policy, dot-product scoring, loss and optimizer fixed; synchronize predictor behavior.

@@ -172,4 +172,12 @@
 
 
+class SmoothNormItemEmbedding(nn.Embedding):
+    def forward(self, items: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
+        embeddings = super().forward(items)
+        squared_norm = embeddings.square().sum(dim=-1, keepdim=True)
+        embeddings = embeddings * torch.rsqrt(1.0 + squared_norm)
+        return embeddings.masked_fill((items == 0).unsqueeze(-1), 0.0)

category_rationales.rationale: Apply smooth norm compression e/sqrt(1+||e||²) to tied item embeddings in all four category models. This preserves small-embedding magnitude differences while limiting large norms. History, target and candidate lookups share the transformation, with padding exactly zero. Dimension, input scaling, HSTU topology, scoring, loss and optimizer remain unchanged. The predictor writer already imports HSTURec from train.py, so inference automatically uses the same transformation with unchanged checkpoint
